title: Consumption-based pricing, pricing models and serverless
learningObjective: Explain the consumption-based model (CapEx vs OpEx), compare Azure pricing models, and describe serverless computing.
foundation: Capital expenditure (CapEx): a large, up-front purchase of something you own, such as servers, paid once and depreciated over years.
Operational expenditure (OpEx): spending on services as you use them, billed regularly. Cloud computing is OpEx.

Consumption-based model: no up-front cost, pay only for what you use, stop paying when you stop using it. You don't buy capacity for the busiest day of the year and leave it idle the rest of the time.
Serverless: you don't manage servers at all. You give Azure your code or workflow, it runs when triggered, scales automatically, and you pay only while it runs.
engineer: Consumption model benefits: no up-front infrastructure cost; no need to buy and manage infrastructure you might not use; pay for additional resources when needed; stop paying when you no longer need them.

Pricing models compared: pay-as-you-go (per second/hour, no commitment); Azure Reservations (commit to specific resources for 1 or 3 years for a discount); Azure savings plan for compute (commit to an hourly compute spend for 1 or 3 years, flexible across sizes and regions); Spot VMs (discounted spare capacity that can be evicted); Azure Hybrid Benefit (reuse eligible Windows Server and SQL Server licences).

Choosing: unknown or short-lived usage → pay-as-you-go. Steady, predictable usage of one resource → reservation. Steady spend but changing resources → savings plan. Interruptible batch → spot. Existing licences → Hybrid Benefit. They can be combined.

Serverless on Azure: Azure Functions (event-driven code: an HTTP request, a queue message, a timer, a new blob), Azure Logic Apps (low-code workflows with connectors), and serverless containers in Azure Container Apps. On consumption plans, billing is per execution and resources consumed, and they can scale to zero.
Serverless still has servers: the provider manages them, their patching and scaling. You focus on code and business logic.
Cost visibility: the pricing calculator estimates before you deploy; Cost Management shows actual spend afterwards.

example.title: Ticket sales spikes
body: A concert promoter sells tickets for a few hours when shows are announced. Owning servers for that peak (CapEx) would leave them idle for weeks.
In Azure, the web tier autoscales on pay-as-you-go, the steady database uses a 3-year reservation, and confirmation emails are sent by an Azure Function billed per execution.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
limits: Reservations and savings plans are commitments: refunds and exchanges have limits
Spot VMs can be evicted with 30 seconds' notice
portal: Pricing calculator: add a VM and compare pay-as-you-go with 1-year and 3-year reserved prices.
Reservations > Add: purchase options (scope, term, billing frequency).
Function App > Create > Hosting: choose a consumption-based plan.

troubleshooting.cause: The reserved VM size or region no longer matches what runs.
troubleshooting.fix: Exchange the reservation or use a savings plan for flexibility.

troubleshooting.symptom: A Spot VM disappeared during a job.
troubleshooting.cause: Azure evicted it to reclaim capacity.
troubleshooting.fix: Use spot only for interruptible work, with checkpoints.

comparisons.difference: Reservations target specific resources; savings plans commit to an hourly spend across eligible compute.
A web app on a dedicated plan is billed while the plan exists; consumption serverless is billed per execution.

misconceptions.myth: Serverless means there are no servers.

misconceptions.reality: Steady workloads may need reservations to be cost-effective; unused resources still cost money.
Budgets, alerts and forecasts make spend predictable.

architectureDecisions: Start on pay-as-you-go, then commit once usage is stable.
Use serverless for event-driven, spiky workloads.
Apply Hybrid Benefit wherever you own eligible licences.
